title: Stage 4: The hotfix backport
summary: 16:00. Production (release/3.1) charges VAT twice on discounted items. The fix is on main; copy exactly that commit to the release branch.

steps.title: Briefing
body: Support reports double VAT in production. Production runs `release/3.1`. Marco already fixed it on `main` (commit `f1x` *fix: apply VAT once [backport]*), but `main` also contains features not ready to ship.
You need **only** `f1x` on `release/3.1`, recorded so anyone can trace it back:

steps.prompt: After `git cherry-pick -x f1x` on `release/3.1`, what does `git log --format=%B -1` print? (The full message of the new commit. The full hash of f1x is `f1x0000`.)
steps.explain: `-x` appends a blank line and the trailer naming the original commit, so the backport is traceable from the release branch.

steps.prompt: Why cherry-pick instead of merging `main` into `release/3.1`?
options: Merging would bring G and H, unreleased features, into production; cherry-pick copies only the fix
Merging is not allowed into release branches
steps.explain: Release branches take selected fixes only. The same fix then exists twice (f1x on main, f1x' on release), which merges cleanly later if ever needed.
Only fixes for bugs in the released version, flagged by whoever fixed them. Features and refactors wait for the next release.

steps.prompt: The release was `v3.1.0`. You add one backported fix and tag. What is the new tag? (Semantic versioning.)
steps.explain: A backwards-compatible bug fix bumps PATCH only.

steps.title: Backport the missing fixes and tag 3.1.1
prompt: In `~/shop`, fixes meant for production are marked `[backport]` in their subject on `main`. One of them was backported last week; the others were not. Your local `release/3.1` is behind the server.
1. Bring `release/3.1` up to date with the server first.
2. Find the `[backport]` fixes on `main` that `release/3.1` does **not** have yet. `git cherry -v release/3.1 main` marks commits whose change is already there with `-`, missing ones with `+`.
3. Cherry-pick each missing one with `-x`, oldest first. Nothing else from `main`.
4. Push `release/3.1`, then tag it `v3.1.1` (annotated, message `Release 3.1.1`) and push the tag.

checks.name: both missing fixes are backported with -x
checks.cmd: cd /srv/git/shop.git && git log --format=%B release/3.1 | grep -qF "(cherry picked from commit $(cat /opt/dojo/state/f1x))" && git log --format=%B release/3.1 | grep -qF "(cherry picked from commit $(cat /opt/dojo/state/empty))"
checks.fail: The server's `release/3.1` should have `fix: apply VAT once` and `fix: guard against an empty basket`, each with its `(cherry picked from commit ...)` line.

checks.name: nothing else came along
checks.cmd: cd /srv/git/shop.git && test "$(git log --format=%s release/3.1 | grep -c 'round refunds')" = 1 && ! git log --format=%s release/3.1 | grep -qE 'feat: gift cards|typo on the admin page'
checks.fail: The refund fix must not be applied twice (it was backported already), and features or non-backport fixes must stay off the release branch.

checks.name: the server's history kept the docs commit
checks.cmd: cd /srv/git/shop.git && git log --format=%s release/3.1 | grep -qx 'docs: 3.1 release notes'
checks.fail: The server's `release/3.1` lost a commit. Update your local branch first (`git pull --rebase` on `release/3.1`), never force-push a release branch.

checks.name: v3.1.1 is an annotated tag on the release tip
checks.cmd: cd /srv/git/shop.git && test "$(git cat-file -t v3.1.1 2>/dev/null)" = tag && test "$(git rev-parse 'v3.1.1^{commit}')" = "$(git rev-parse release/3.1)"
checks.fail: Push an annotated tag `v3.1.1` that points at the new tip of `release/3.1`: `git tag -a v3.1.1 -m "Release 3.1.1"` and `git push origin v3.1.1`.

hints: `git switch release/3.1` and `git pull --rebase` (or `git merge --ff-only origin/release/3.1`).
`git cherry -v release/3.1 main | grep backport` shows `+` for the two that are missing and `-` for the refund fix.
`git cherry-pick -x <vat hash> <basket hash>`, `git push`, `git tag -a v3.1.1 -m "Release 3.1.1"`, `git push origin v3.1.1`.
solution: git cherry-pick -x $(git cherry release/3.1 main | awk '$1 == "+" {print $2}' | while read c; do git log -1 --format='%H %s' "$c"; done | grep backport | cut -d' ' -f1)
steps.explain: `git cherry` compares by **patch id** (the change itself), so it recognises a commit that was cherry-picked with a new hash. That is how release managers answer "what is still missing on the release branch?" without trusting memory or ticket comments. Pull before you pick: a stale release branch is how the same fix gets applied twice.
